clue.text: Monopoly requirement: five hundred diamonds

blocks.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A board-game rule book listing what a Monopoly tycoon needs: five hundred in cash and some jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: Players of the board game Monopoly roll a pair of these cubes to move their tokens round the board.

clue.text: Design heretical credo

indicators.note: a heretical belief departs from orthodoxy, so these letters depart from their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Drafting a creed that the church would condemn.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the style of furnishing and decoration of a room, its interior design.

clue.text: Bucking bronco swallows bit of compostable food scrap

indicators.note: a bucking horse throws itself about, so these letters are tossed into another order
just a small bit of the word is taken, its opening letter
what swallows something takes it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A wild horse gulping down kitchen waste meant for the compost heap.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled BRONCO takes in the C: CORN-C-OB.
explanation.definitionFit: A corncob is the woody core left after the kernels are eaten, a scrap thrown away after a meal.

clue.text: Generous one moving in two pieces of furniture

indicators.note: the single letter standing for one shifts its position, so the furniture spelling is rearranged slightly

blocks.note: a chair and a table, set side by side

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted person helping a neighbour shift furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: Write CHAIR TABLE, then move the I (one) one place along: CHAR-I-TABLE gives CHARITABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable describes someone who gives freely to others, a close synonym of generous.

clue.text: Exotic oriole in Her Majesty's legacy

indicators.note: something exotic is strange and foreign, so these letters take on an unfamiliar arrangement
one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: HM is the abbreviation for Her Majesty
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rare foreign songbird kept in the Queen's collection and passed down.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled ORIOLE sits between the H and M: H-EIRLOO-M.
explanation.definitionFit: An heirloom is a valued possession handed down through generations, something left as a legacy.

clue.text: Irritate right part of the leg

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
the joint at the bottom of the leg

explanation.surface: Something annoying the right leg.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle is to cause lasting resentment or annoyance, so it means to irritate.

clue.text: Trumpet to purchase in place of a piece of wood

indicators.note: to trumpet is to proclaim out loud, so the words that follow are judged by their sound

blocks.note: the little word said out loud
to purchase is to buy
for means in place of, as in swapping one for another

explanation.surface: An advertisement urging people to buy something instead of a plank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trumpet' looks like a musical instrument, but it is a verb meaning proclaim: TO BUY FOR, said out loud, is TWO-BY-FOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-by-four is a standard length of sawn lumber measuring two inches by four in cross-section.

clue.text: Plot wicked trouble

blocks.note: a plot of garden ground, such as a flower bed
wicked means evil

explanation.surface: A villain's scheme to cause mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' wants to be a scheme, but here it is a patch of garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedevil is to plague or harass persistently, which is to trouble someone.

clue.text: Sorry, reels got tangled up — unlike this clue

indicators.note: something tangled up is knotted into disorder, so these letters come out in a jumble
the answer is flawless while the clue is not, so the clue's one faulty letter has to be thrown out

blocks.note: taken as written; one of these letters is surplus, which is the joke

explanation.surface: An apology for a fishing line or film reel that has become knotted.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder has one letter too many, a Y, and that is the point: the clue contains an error, so the flawless answer is 'unlike this clue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Errorless means without any mistake, the opposite of a clue that deliberately contains a slip.

clue.text: Father's time!

blocks.note: Pa is father, so father's is PA'S
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a father's time, the era of one's parents, is gone by, and the exclamation mark flags the double reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The generation of one's father belongs to bygone days, which is what the past means.

clue.text: Pink auto country

blocks.note: an auto is a car
a country is a nation

explanation.surface: Reads like a description of a pink-coloured car from some country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pink' looks like a colour adjective, but here it is the noun for a garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinks are a family of flowers (Dianthus), and the carnation is the best-known member of that family.

clue.text: See 18
Article reviewed concert

indicators.note: something reviewed is looked at again and reworked, so these letters are put in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece giving a critic's verdict on a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical performance, usually by a soloist or small group, so it is a kind of concert.

clue.text: Amy, losing heart during paramour's travel break

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle of the name drops out, leaving only its ends
something happening during another thing sits within it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a paramour is an illicit lover
the name with its middle letter removed

explanation.surface: Amy, heartbroken, while away on a trip with her lover.
explanation.walkthrough: A paramour is a secret lover; 'losing heart' strips the middle from a name, not an emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A layover is a stop between legs of a journey, a pause or break in travel.

clue.text: Bravo — it's "quavers"!

indicators.note: to quaver is to tremble or waver, so the letters before it shake loose into a new order; the word doubles as the definition

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A concert-goer applauding a singer's trills.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks hint that 'quavers' does two jobs: it shakes up BRAVO IT'S and it defines the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibratos are the pulsating wavers in a sung or played note, which is what quavers in a voice are.

clue.text: Law-enforcement team that might investigate Biden's muscle

blocks.note: when this puzzle appeared Joe Biden was the US Vice President, so he is VICE, with the possessive S
a quad is a quadriceps, the big thigh muscle

explanation.surface: Imagines police officers looking into the strength of the then Vice President.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2012 Joe Biden was Vice President, so the clue treats him as VICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice squad is a police unit dealing with gambling, prostitution and drugs, a law-enforcement team.

clue.text: Hiking mineshaft in Arizona town leads to the other side of the world

definitions.text: the other side of the world

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other
hiking goes uphill, and in a down entry going up means reading from the bottom

blocks.note: Sedona is a town in Arizona known for its red rocks
a pit is a mineshaft

explanation.surface: A hiker in Arizona finds a mineshaft that seems to tunnel right through the Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'hiking' (going up) means the whole construction is read from the bottom upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The antipodes are places diametrically opposite on the globe, often meaning Australia and New Zealand.

clue.text: Try a fairy tale with soccer player

blocks.note: to have a go is to have a try
taken as written
a fairy tale, in the sense of a made-up story, is a lie

explanation.surface: An instruction to attempt a storybook tale starring a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalie is the goalkeeper, the soccer player who guards the net.

clue.text: Everyone is into bogus pearl analogy

indicators.note: something bogus is fake, so these letters are rearranged into a counterfeit
one thing being into another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
everyone is all

explanation.surface: Everybody loves a comparison likening something to a fake pearl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Everyone is' reads as the sentence's subject, but it is the inserted piece and its placement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A parallel is a comparison drawing a likeness between two things, which is what an analogy is.

clue.text: Ask for decorum and phone the pizza parlor?

blocks.note: first meaning: what a chairperson does to quiet a meeting
second meaning, read literally

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, playful reading of the phrase as a phone call made to order food.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the formal term for opening or restoring discipline at a meeting, and literally a call made so as to order something.

clue.text: Radiant, gentle beast dispatched without a head

indicators.note: being headless means the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: a lamb is the proverbially gentle animal
dispatched means sent

explanation.surface: A shining, mild animal that has been killed and beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispatched' suggests killed, but here it means sent.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent describes light that softly glows or flickers, so it means radiant.

clue.text: Forbid torture devices in military facility

blocks.note: to bar is to forbid
racks are frames for stretching victims

explanation.surface: A call to ban instruments of torture on army bases.
explanation.definitionFit: Barracks are the buildings where soldiers are housed on a military base.

clue.text: God's nuclear reactor

indicators.note: the word nuclear is itself a jumble of unclear, hinting that the next word is to be muddled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Imagines the Almighty owning a nuclear power plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. 'Nuclear' reads as part of the power plant, but it signals a mix-up, being a mix-up of 'unclear'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Creator is a title for God as maker of the universe.

clue.text: Puzzler's kid raising gold

indicators.note: raising lifts something up, and in a down entry that reads it from the bottom

blocks.note: to kid is to josh, to tease
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A setter's child lifting up something golden.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzler is Joshua Kosman, one of this puzzle's two setters; 's stands for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Joshua Kosman co-sets The Nation's cryptic, so he is the puzzler meant here.

clue.text: Part-time athlete's failed promise

indicators.note: something that has failed has broken down, so these letters fall apart and are rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The disappointment of a weekend sportsman who never fulfilled his early potential.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A semipro is a semi-professional, paid to play but not full-time, so a part-time athlete.

clue.text: Increase toxic mutagen

indicators.note: something toxic is poisoned and corrupted, so these letters are spoilt into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lab warning to boost the dose of a poisonous agent that causes mutations.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment is to make larger or add to, a formal synonym of increase.

clue.text: Dress for the general public to have

blocks.note: G is the US film rating meaning suitable for general audiences
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Clothing made available for ordinary people to possess.
explanation.walkthrough: G is the American film rating for General Audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: A gown is a long formal dress.

clue.text: Suitors offer to carry trunk

indicators.note: the words before it carry the answer inside their letters

blocks.note: found across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Admirers volunteering to lug a heavy chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests luggage, but here it is the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the body is the torso, the part without head or limbs.

clue.text: Coup endeavors to conceal overthrow

indicators.note: the words before it conceal the answer inside their run of letters

blocks.note: found across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Plotters trying to cover up their seizure of power.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend is to turn upside down or topple, which is what overthrowing something does.

clue.text: Yowl in distress when immersed in enemy's ritual substance

indicators.note: something in distress is in a state of disorder, so these letters are scrambled
something immersed in another is plunged inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: an enemy is a hater
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cat howling as it is dunked in its foe's ceremonial liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yowl' sounds like the cry of a creature in distress, but it is the letters to be jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy water is water blessed by a priest and used in rites such as baptism, a ritual substance.

clue.text: Abominable drive on the shoulders, with defective seat belt

indicators.note: shoulders are the edges of a road, so only the outside letters of the word are kept
something defective is faulty and out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the two edge letters of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A terrible ride along the hard shoulder with a broken seat belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the shoulders' plays on the road shoulder, but it means the word's two edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Detestable means deserving hatred, a direct synonym of abominable.

clue.text: Mythical ship jettisoning 20 percent of merchandise on board

indicators.note: throwing a fifth overboard removes one letter of a five-letter word, here the first

blocks.note: goods carried on a ship

explanation.surface: A legendary vessel lightening its load by throwing a fifth of its goods overboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek legend.
